ISRAEL (THE NORTH): 19 RULERS JEROBOAM I → HOSHEA
ACCESSION
How Jeroboam I came to power

While he was in charge of the labour of “the house of Joseph”, Ahijah the Shilonite tore a new garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten: “I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee”. 1 Kings 11:28–31
Ahijah promised him “a sure house, as I built for David”, if he would walk in God's ways. 1 Kings 11:38
Solomon sought to kill him, and he fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died. 1 Kings 11:40

When Rehoboam refused to lighten the yoke, Israel answered “What portion have we in David?” and made Jeroboam “king over all Israel”; only Judah followed the house of David. 1 Kings 12:16 1 Kings 12:20
Kings gives the cause: “the cause was from the LORD, that he might perform his saying, which the LORD spake by Ahijah the Shilonite”. 1 Kings 12:15
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“Jeroboam returned not from his evil way”
1 Kings 13:33 (KJV) →
“the sins of Jeroboam, who did sin, and who made Israel to sin”
1 Kings 14:16 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO
Ahijah's message to him: “thou hast not been as my servant David” but “hast done evil above all that were before thee”. 1 Kings 14:8–9
His sin becomes the measure for later kings of Israel, almost all of whom “departed not from the sins of Jeroboam”. 2 Kings 10:31
Kings' closing account of the north names him: “Jeroboam drave Israel from following the LORD, and made them sin a great sin”. 2 Kings 17:21

Chronicles adds that he and his sons cast the Levites off from the priest's office, and that he ordained priests “for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made”. 2 Chronicles 11:14–15

UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
Two golden calves, at Beth-el and Dan; “this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan”. 1 Kings 12:28–30
A “house of high places”, priests not of Levi, and a feast of his own in the eighth month. 1 Kings 12:31–33
The priests and Levites left their lands for Judah and Jerusalem, followed by those “such as set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel”. 2 Chronicles 11:13–16

Th The old prophet of Beth-el Deceived the man of God into eating at Beth-el, buried him, and confirmed his word against the altar.
Sh Shemaiah the man of God Stopped Rehoboam's war to win back the north: “this thing is from me”.

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
THIELE, AS REVISED BY MCFALL AND YOUNG
Spring 931 BC to 910/909 BC
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 922–901 (p. 20); 22 years (last digit partly lost in the scan's gutter, read from the next reign's start).
TRADITIONAL (USSHER, 1658)
Begins in the year of the world 3029; Nadab succeeds in 3050 (Annals, pp. 40–42)
About 975 BC
James Ussher, Annals of the World (1658), p. 40
Ussher counted the reign lengths back from later fixed points and set Solomon's death and the division in the year of the world 3029, 975 BC.[2]
About 933 BC
Edward Mack, ISBE (1915), vol. 1, p. 640
Mack worked back from Assyrian fixed points (Jehu's tribute, Qarqar, the fall of Samaria) and allowed for overlapping reigns, placing “the Disruption in 933 BC”.[21]
E. R. Thiele, as revised by L. McFall and R. C. Young (Young's tables)
Thiele's system, as revised by McFall and Young, starts Jeroboam's reign in the spring of 931 BC, with Israel counting a king's first part-year as his year one.[1]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not give his age when he began to reign, or where he was buried.
Kings does not say how he died; Chronicles says only that “the LORD struck him”.
Scripture gives no year of his reign for the calves, the feast or the man of God's visit.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
Scripture introduces him as “Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon’s servant, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow woman”. 1 Kings 11:26
From the textThis page is about Jeroboam son of Nebat. Jeroboam II, son of Joash, who began to reign about 140 years later, has his own page.
